Definition: Does the government maintain a digital address register?
Comments: No national address registry found after searches.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown with no source was mislabelled: a light check surfaced authoritative evidence of an operating address system. Freetown City Council's property reform (underway since 2019/2020) has officially adopted Google Plus Codes as building addresses for its property/business tax database, and in March 2024 the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI) partnered with Google Maps to digitise physical addresses more broadly. Deployment is confirmed in the capital but not shown to be nationwide, so the code is raised from 0 to 4 (Partially deployed).
revised_comments: Sierra Leone has a digital address register in the form of Google Plus Codes, officially adopted by Freetown City Council since its 2019-2020 property tax reform to identify buildings lacking conventional street addresses, and extended through a 2024 partnership between the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI) and Google Maps to digitise physical addresses more widely. Deployment remains concentrated in Freetown and other urban centres rather than covering the whole country.

revision_notes: The original source (OARG business register page) confirms only a manual, paper-based registration process in which a TIN is generated alongside the business registration certificate; it does not evidence connection to a national data exchange/interoperability platform. Fresh evidence shows active reform: the World Bank-funded SL Economic Diversification Project was implementing a One-Stop-Shop for Business Services (targeted for October 2024), and Sierra Leone's Companies and Business Registration Act establishes a Board mandated to operate a One-Stop Shop with a centralised electronic database and legally required data sharing with tax, social security and municipal licensing bodies. Full connection to the broader government data-exchange platform is not yet confirmed as operational, so the code is raised from 1 to 3 (Under development) rather than higher.
revised_comments: Business registration integration with Sierra Leone's wider government data exchange system is under development. A Companies and Business Registration Act establishes a Board mandated to operate a One-Stop Shop with a centralised electronic database and legally required data sharing with the National Revenue Authority, social security and municipal licensing bodies, building on an earlier World Bank-supported One-Stop-Shop for Business Services reform. Full integration with the national interoperability platform has not yet been confirmed as operational.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital land register?
Comments: MLHCP and OARG handle land reg, mining cadastre digital.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: One original source (nma.gov.sl mining cadastre) is unrelated: it describes the Mining Cadastre Administration System used for mineral rights licensing, not the general land title/deeds register, and should not have been cited for this variable. The other (molhcp.gov.sl) is the Ministry's generic homepage with no specific evidence on digitisation status. Fresh evidence from the World Bank's 2022 Land Administration Project appraisal confirms land records remain paper-based (cadastral maps and deeds stored manually; prior 2014 and 2016 digitisation attempts did not progress) and that a new digital Land Information System is only now being developed under the Sierra Leone Land Administration Project (SLLAP, 2022-2028). World Bank Doing Business 2019 data likewise records land records as kept in 'Paper' format. Code revised down from 4 (Partially deployed) to 3 (Under development).
revised_comments: Sierra Leone's land register remains largely paper-based. Cadastral maps and deed records are stored manually across the Office of the Administrator and Registrar General and the Ministry of Lands, Housing and Country Planning, and earlier digitisation attempts in 2014 and 2016 did not progress. A modern digital Land Information System is under development through the World Bank-financed Sierra Leone Land Administration Project (2022-2028), which aims to unify the land registry and cadastre and enable electronic data exchange, but it is not yet operational.

redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Both original sources could not be verified: the NaCSA page returned a 403 access error and the World Bank blog on digital ID does not report a social registry coverage figure. Cross-referencing World Bank Social Safety Net project documents and the 2021 Public Expenditure Review: Sierra Leone's core Ep Fet Po cash transfer programme (whose targeting data populates the SPRINT social registry) covered around 65,000 extremely poor households by mid-2022, against a national extreme poverty rate of 12.85% (SLIHS 2018) implying roughly 250,000-270,000 extremely poor households nationwide — a coverage rate in the region of 20-30%. This supports the original 20-49% band, so the score of 2 is confirmed rather than changed, albeit with materially better sourcing.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone's social protection registry (SPRINT), built on the National Commission for Social Action's Ep Fet Po cash transfer programme, covers an estimated one-fifth to one-third of intended beneficiaries. As of mid-2022 the core programme supported around 65,000 extremely poor households, against a national extreme poverty rate of around 13% implying a target population of roughly 250,000-270,000 extremely poor households, indicating partial but incomplete coverage of the intended beneficiary population.
